races.name: Oliver Brown Pretty Polly Stakes (Listed Race) (Fillies)

runners_data.name: Maldives
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with expensive pedigree making just third career start, lacks experience for this tactical battle.
runners_data.comment: 2,900,000gns yearling by Camelot; hampered when second in novice at Yarmouth (1m2f, good)
runners_data.spotlight: 2,900,000gns yearling by Camelot; first foal of Group-placed 7f 2yo winner (RPR 102), herself a half-sister to multiple Group 1 winner Luxembourg; 8-1 in steadily run novice at Yarmouth (1m2f, good) three weeks ago, short of room for a sustained period before running on into second of seven; Irish Oaks entry who is bottom on ratings but probably capable of a lot better.

runners_data.name: Esna
runners_data.note: Prominent style with strong Group-class form but concerning 210-day absence since last run.
runners_data.comment: Clear top on form after her Group 1 Marcel Boussac fourth; fair chance she'll stay 1m2f
runners_data.spotlight: All three starts as 2yo were on soft; green in front in 7f novice win at Sandown against a notable rival; about 2l fourth of eight when an outsider for 1m Group 1 Marcel Boussac at Longchamp, keeping on well while never able to threaten seriously the lead; fair chance she'll stay 1m2f, judged on that, even if pedigree (sire sprinter) casts doubts on her Oaks entry; clear top on form.

runners_data.name: Lilt
runners_data.note: Front-runner returning from 191-day break with limited experience, vulnerable in this pace battle.
runners_data.comment: 7f Doncaster maiden win as 2yo is just fair form but she looks the type to do a lot better
runners_data.spotlight: Lope De Vega half-sister to winners Doom (7f/1m including Listed; RPR 104) and Kilt (1m; 97); dam a well-related 1m-1m2f winner (including US Grade 1; 116); 7-2 for a six-runner maiden at Doncaster (7f, soft) in October, dictating a steady pace and battling on well to win by a neck; that's just fair form but this 1m Coronation Stakes and 1m4f Irish Oaks entry looks the type to do a lot better as 3yo.

runners_data.name: Sacred Ground
runners_data.note: Leading contender with front-running style, best form, and strong Gosden stable behind her.
runners_data.comment: By Kingman out of Oaks winner Anapurna; won debut and second of ten in 1m Listed race here
runners_data.spotlight: By Kingman out of Oaks winner Anapurna; favourite for both starts as 2yo, overcoming greenness to win a five-runner novice at Yarmouth (1m, good to firm) and every chance through the final 3f when second of ten in Listed race at Newmarket (1m, good to soft); Oaks entry from a stable which has a fine record in this race and houses the current Oaks favourite, so market strength would probably be telling.

runners_data.name: Spinning Lizzie
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist perfectly positioned to benefit from the expected strong pace, recent AW win shows current form.
runners_data.comment: Has come up short in her three Group events and the same is likely to be the case today
runners_data.spotlight: Won debut as 2yo but twice came up short in Group events; resumed with a late charge to grab a conditions stakes at Kempton (1m, AW) in March but the Group 3 Fred Darling at Newbury (7f, good; 22-1, made most) proved too tough and, despite a new trip, the same is likely to be the case today.

runners_data.name: Jennifer Jane
runners_data.note: Proven front-runner but 252 days since last outing raises fitness concerns in this competitive heat.
runners_data.comment: Good chance she will stay 1m2f; needs to resume progress after last in a Group 3 in August
runners_data.spotlight: Made all in a maiden at Wetherby (7f, good to firm) on second start and almost all in Listed race at Sandown (7f, good) later last summer; her season ended, however, with last of seven in Group 3 at Goodwood (7f, good to firm) in August; good chance she will stay 1m2f; needs to resume progress.

runners_data.name: Brigid's Well
runners_data.note: Front-running style adds to pace pressure but lacks the class to sustain the gallop against stronger rivals.
runners_data.comment: 11-1 fourth of ten in 1m Listed race here on final 2yo start, with Sacred Ground in second
runners_data.spotlight: Made all in one 1m novice as a 2yo and very nearly did so in another; 11-1 fourth of ten in Listed race here (1m, good to soft; Sacred Ground was second) on final start illustrated some limitations, sticking to her task well as if this longer trip would suit but, despite the Oaks entry, she probably has serious work to do in this company too.

races.paceDynamic: Lilt, Sacred Ground, Jennifer Jane, and Brigid's Well will all want to lead from the start, creating a genuine speed battle in the early stages. With four confirmed front-runners in a small field of seven, this guarantees a strong pace throughout the 1m2f trip. The sustained gallop will stretch the field and test stamina reserves to the maximum. This setup strongly favours hold-up horses and those with proven staying power who can benefit from the collapse of over-exerted pace-setters.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Benefits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the four front-runners engage in their expected speed duel from the start
scenarios.body: The strong early gallop will cause several pace-setters to weaken dramatically in the final furlong, allowing horses held up off the pace to sweep past tired leaders. Spinning Lizzie's hold-up style and Esna's class will prove decisive when others have shot their bolt.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Pace-Setter Survives
scenarios.trigger: If Sacred Ground or Jennifer Jane can steal a march on their pace rivals
scenarios.body: The Gosden-trained Sacred Ground has the class and breeding to outlast her speed rivals, while Jennifer Jane's front-running experience could see her dominate weaker opposition. Their superior ratings give them the edge if they can control the tempo.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Maldives or Esna can position perfectly behind the speed battle
scenarios.body: The prominent runners will have the perfect position to strike when the leaders weaken, tracking the pace without being caught up in the early burn. Maldives's expensive pedigree and Esna's Group-class form make them dangerous if positioned right.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos and Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the pace somehow becomes more moderate than expected
scenarios.body: The tactical battle becomes less clear-cut and form horses can assert their superiority through pure ability. This unlikely scenario would suit horses with versatile styles who can adapt to changing race dynamics.

watchPoints.text: Sacred Ground and Jennifer Jane both want to lead - watch for early positioning battle that could compromise both
Esna returns from 210-day break - monitor market confidence and paddock demeanor for fitness clues
Four confirmed front-runners in seven-horse field - expect unusually strong pace from flag-fall
Spinning Lizzie's hold-up style against strong pace - watch for typical patient ride from Rossa Ryan
Maldives making only third start in Listed company - observe if inexperience shows under pressure

races.name: Betfred Dahlia Stakes (Group 2) (Fillies & Mares)

runners_data.name: Cathedral
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who needs strong pace to be effective, 36 days off may leave her short of peak fitness
runners_data.comment: Form includes three good efforts at Group/Grade 1 level; leading player on ratings
runners_data.spotlight: Possibly unsuited by soft ground; record of 0-8 since debut success doesn't do her justice, with three good efforts at Group/Grade 1 level (1m/1m3f) among her form; leading player on ratings returned to turf with AW reappearance under her belt.

runners_data.name: American Gal
runners_data.note: Prominent runner whose form has declined since good second at Ascot, this represents a significant step up
runners_data.comment: Not in the same form since close second in Ascot Group 3 on King George day
runners_data.spotlight: Steady progress culminated in close second to Cheshire Dancer in Group 3 at Ascot (1m) on King George day last year; not in the same form since and this is a stiff task even if she rebounds.

runners_data.name: Miss Justice
runners_data.note: Prominent type changing hands to Brian Meehan, 205 days off is a major concern despite previous ability
runners_data.comment: Close second at Newmarket on final start for the Gosdens; sold 750,000gns since
runners_data.spotlight: Form for the Gosdens featured a Listed win last August and close second in Newmarket Group 3 in October (both 1m2f); sold for 750,000gns since; this is harder but she may do better still.

runners_data.name: Chantilly Lace
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with strong Group race form, 228-day layoff makes her hard to assess confidently
runners_data.comment: Lightly raced; consistent until below par on last appearance; may rebound
runners_data.spotlight: Lightly raced; good fifth in the 1,000 Guineas and Coronation Stakes prior to close third in Ascot Group 3 won by Cheshire Dancer; below par in final 3yo start but consistent otherwise and may rebound.

runners_data.name: Survie
runners_data.note: Strong hold-up performer who prefers longer trips, the drop back to 1m1f is a tactical negative
runners_data.comment: Has several pieces of Group 1 form, including Saudi effort for new yard; big player
runners_data.spotlight: Ex-French mare who has several pieces of Group 1 form over middle distances, including a Saudi effort since joining new yard this year; unsuited by drop back to 1m last time when one place behind Cathedral, losing her unbeaten AW record; big player on peak figures.

runners_data.name: Jancis
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who hasn't won since early career, 177 days off adds to her chances appearing limited
runners_data.comment: Useful sort but looks unlikely to regain the winning thread in this field
runners_data.spotlight: Irish mare whose career commenced with two Leopardstown wins, including in Group 3; 0-7 since but has continued to show useful form; unlikely to get back on the scoresheet in this field, however.

runners_data.name: Sand Gazelle
runners_data.note: Hold-up type from powerful Gosden stable, 205-day absence but yard's 11/39 record provides confidence
runners_data.comment: Low-mileage filly; broadly progressive and may have more to offer this term
runners_data.spotlight: Low-mileage filly; below form at Newmarket when last seen but broadly progressive otherwise and may have more to offer this term; Listed winner at York (1m2f) last July then ran well in Group 3 at the Curragh (1m1f); shortlisted.

runners_data.name: Arisaig
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in good current form, just 1 day since last run gives her a significant fitness advantage
runners_data.comment: Reliable mare who should go well again back in a Listed event but her last win was in 2024
runners_data.spotlight: Talented mare who ran well in Listed and Group events last season and was runner-up in a Class 2 handicap at Newmarket (1m, good) on her reappearance last month; should go well again but she has a bit to find on these figures and her last win was in July 2024.

runners_data.name: Francophone
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with Listed wins but overall record suggests she's below this grade
runners_data.comment: Listed win at Newmarket on last appearance; unlikely to follow up in this grade
runners_data.spotlight: Successful twice in Listed grade, including at Newmarket (1m, good to firm) on last appearance; could go well but her overall record and ratings suggest she's unlikely to follow up in this better race.

runners_data.name: Qilin Queen
runners_data.note: Non-runner, prominent type who may not get the trip anyway
runners_data.comment: Group 2 winner on French soil but this is a stronger contest for the level
runners_data.spotlight: Scored at Longchamp (1m4f, good to soft) in sole Group 2 attempt but this is a stronger contest for the level and today's trip may be inadequate; one for other days with this reappearance under her belt.

runners_data.name: Falakeyah
runners_data.note: Lone front-runner whose headstrong nature could work for or against her depending on settling
runners_data.comment: Looks worth another chance to confirm the high promise of her win on this card last year
runners_data.spotlight: Has proved headstrong and she was disappointing in last two appearances, including when only 5-2 for the Coronation Stakes having bypassed the Oaks and French Oaks, but this may be the time to catch her; comfortably justified favouritism in the Pretty Polly on this card (good to firm) 12 months ago, taking record to 2-2 and looking a potentially high-class filly; worth another chance.

runners_data.name: Cheshire Dancer
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with excellent Group 3 form, 211-day break is the main concern
runners_data.comment: Chance of landing this prize depends on the effects of first-time headgear
runners_data.spotlight: Developed into a very useful sort last term, notably Group/Grade 3 performances at Ascot (won) and Kentucky Downs (ran well); chance of landing this prize depends on the effects of first-time headgear.

runners_data.name: Stateira
runners_data.note: Hold-up type better on AW surfaces, switching from Newcastle success to Newmarket turf is questionable
runners_data.comment: Doing well on AW but is far from certain to sustain her progress back on turf
runners_data.spotlight: Doing well on AW and justified favouritism in 7f handicap on finals day, taking Newcastle record to 3-3; far from certain to sustain her progress over this longer trip back on turf (second attempt in this sphere).

races.paceDynamic: Falakeyah is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 13-runner Group 2, creating a tactical advantage as she can dictate terms without early pressure. American Gal and Miss Justice will likely sit prominent behind her, but neither appears keen to challenge for the early lead. The moderate early gallop will produce a sustained finish over the final 3-4 furlongs on Newmarket's uphill climb. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can produce late kicks, as the uncontested leader may weaken and the patient finishers will have every chance to strike.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Kicks
scenarios.trigger: If Falakeyah gets an easy lead and finds her rhythm without early harassment
scenarios.body: The headstrong filly settles better than recent runs and has enough left to repel late challenges up the hill. Her tactical advantage of controlling the pace from the front proves decisive when the closers make their moves.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely modest and Falakeyah's stamina cracks in the final furlong
scenarios.body: The patient finishers get perfect racing room as the field spreads out, with Cathedral and Survie producing the strongest late kicks. Multiple hold-up horses sweep past the weakening pace-setter in the final 100 yards.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Duo Strike
scenarios.trigger: If American Gal or Miss Justice decides to challenge Falakeyah approaching the 2f marker
scenarios.body: The early move puts pressure on the leader while staying clear of the traffic behind, creating a winning move before the hold-up horses can respond. One of the prominent runners sustains their effort better than expected.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Falakeyah stops completely and the prominent horses also weaken dramatically
scenarios.body: The entire pace collapses leaving a sprint finish from the back markers, with traffic problems and hard luck stories throughout. The winner emerges from the pack having been stone last turning for home.

watchPoints.text: Falakeyah must settle early or her chance disappears completely given her recent headstrong displays
Cathedral and Survie need the pace to develop strongly enough to play to their hold-up running styles
Miss Justice making her debut for new trainer Meehan after 205 days off could be rusty despite ability
Multiple hold-up horses including Sand Gazelle and Cheshire Dancer return from 200+ day layoffs
Arisaig has the fitness edge running just 1 day after her Newmarket second in handicap company

races.name: Betfred Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Yashin
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer returning after 232 days with excellent fresh record but needs the gaps to open late
runners_data.comment: Started 2025 with a bang (won slowly run Group 3) but there was only a whimper afterwards
runners_data.spotlight: Started 2025 with a bang for new connections when winning a slowly run, four-runner Group 3 at Ascot (2m, good to firm) in April; remote with ambitious targets on next three starts and although sixth of 11 in 2m handicap at Chester in September was an upturn, markedly better is required to win this..

runners_data.name: Goblet Of Fire
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who prefers AW to turf based on strike-rates, each-way claims if adapting
runners_data.comment: Has a run under his belt but to win this would require a new best performance on turf
runners_data.spotlight: All of his Flat success for this yard has been on AW, albeit with good-ground hurdle wins too and he was runner-up at Goodwood (1m6f, good to firm) last August; has a run under his belt this term but to win this would require a new best performance on turf.

runners_data.name: Subsequent
runners_data.note: Quality hold-up horse with Listed form who found career-best level when last seen 233 days ago
runners_data.comment: Yorkshire Cup and Ascot Gold Cup entries are striking but ground softer than good is ideal
runners_data.spotlight: Excellent 3yo season culminated in his Listed win at Ascot (1m6f, soft) and, after a delayed reappearance last year, he found career-best form to win a good handicap at Doncaster (14.5f, good to soft; tongue tied second time) in September on final outing; the Yorkshire Cup and Ascot Gold Cup entries are striking but ideally he would be on ground softer than good.

runners_data.name: Align The Stars
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in excellent current form with cheekpieces restored and clear fitness edge
runners_data.comment: May have turned a corner when he broke his losing run in clearcut style at Kempton (AW)
runners_data.spotlight: Thereabouts on occasions in 2025, crept down the weights and broke his losing run in clearcut style when he reappeared five weeks ago wearing restored cheekpieces in the Queen's Prize at Kempton (2m, AW); back up 4lb but showed plenty of bottle in that win and may have turned a corner.

runners_data.name: Pole Star
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with strong 1m6f record but question marks over readiness for this grade
runners_data.comment: Just 15-8 when fading into 4th of six at Newbury (2m); visor and back down in trip
runners_data.spotlight: Won two 1m6f handicaps last term and two respectable efforts in valuable races in late summer; just 10-1 for 2m2f Cesarewitch at Newmarket on final 3yo outing, which did not work out, and he was just 15-8 when fading into fourth of six at Newbury (2m) 16 days ago on first run since he was gelded; connections now turn to a visor and drop him back in trip.

runners_data.name: Dramatic Star
runners_data.note: Hold-up type wearing first-time headgear after disappointing recent efforts, each-way appeal
runners_data.comment: E-w claims if back to best with first-time headgear after two rather disappointing runs
runners_data.spotlight: Improved last year without quite winning; each-way claims if back to best with first-time headgear after two rather disappointing runs in 2026.

runners_data.name: Charging Thunder
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer whose recent Beverley second demands significant improvement here
runners_data.comment: 2nd of 5 when returned to Flat turf at Beverley (2m) 18 days ago; this demands much more
runners_data.spotlight: Had underwhelming hurdle and AW campaigns before his second of five when returned to Flat turf at Beverley (2m) 18 days ago; this demands markedly better and his 2024 and 2025 turf records aren't that persuasive.

runners_data.name: Brasil Power
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with solid recent 1m4f+ form but struggles in this level of competition
runners_data.comment: This race perhaps too tough; no turf form (admittedly at up to 1m2f) is close to this mark
runners_data.spotlight: Moving up to 1m4f worked well in December and comparable form at 1m6f/2m since, including another win three starts back; he's come up a bit short in warmer races this year, though, including behind Align The Stars at Kempton, and none of his turf form (admittedly at up to 1m2f) is close to this mark.

runners_data.name: Many Men
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with excellent 2024 progress including three handicap wins, major player
runners_data.comment: Excellent progress as 3yo; well below best on 2026 return but that may have put him right
runners_data.spotlight: Excellent progress last term included three handicap wins (1m2f, 1m6f and 2m) in March-July and an agonisingly close call in the Melrose at York in August; close fourth in 1m6f Listed race at Ascot on final outing; well below that form on 2026 reappearance but that may have put him right.

runners_data.name: Kihavah
runners_data.note: Only confirmed front runner who will dictate pace and proved much better in this race last year
runners_data.comment: Saw daylight all too late when strong-finishing 5th in this race last year off 4lb higher
runners_data.spotlight: Saw daylight all too late when strong-finishing fifth in this race last year (much better than his 2024 performance in it); Meydan this January/February did not yield much (stiff tasks) but he's now 4lb lower than this time last year, too well handicapped to be ruled out; rare run in cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: Artisan Dancer
runners_data.note: Hold-up type fit from AW but poor 1-17 turf strike-rate makes him vulnerable despite consistency
runners_data.comment: Industrious and dependable sort over 1m6f-2m2f but his turf strike-rate is just 1-17
runners_data.spotlight: Industrious and dependable sort over 1m6f-2m2f, who's fit from AW, but his turf strike-rate is just 1-17 and that makes him look vulnerable.

runners_data.name: Bahadur
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with hat-trick confidence from AW but questions remain about turf effectiveness
runners_data.comment: Made immediate progress when switched to AW in the autumn; needs to show show same on turf
runners_data.spotlight: Made immediate progress when switched to AW in the autumn, completing a hat-trick in a 1m4f novice and 1m4f/1m6f handicaps; perhaps in need of the race (albeit joint-favourite) on reappearance four weeks ago, but now needs to show that he can serve up his best on turf.

races.paceDynamic: Kihavah is the only confirmed front runner in this field and will dictate from the start, likely setting a manageable gallop over the extended trip. Align The Stars and Bahadur as prominent runners may track close but won't apply serious early pressure. The majority field of hold-up horses including Yashin, Subsequent, Many Men and Pole Star will settle behind in the large pack, creating a bunched field turning for home. This tactical setup strongly favours hold-up performers who can produce late kicks, as they'll have clear racing room when the pace inevitably quickens in the final three furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Front Running
scenarios.trigger: If Kihavah gets soft sectionals and isn't pressed early.
scenarios.body: The veteran can dictate completely and prove hard to peg back despite the quality behind. His style becomes a major asset when he controls the tempo from flag to finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Strong Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the hold-up brigade get the splits they need turning in.
scenarios.body: Quality closers like Yashin and Subsequent can unleash superior finishing kicks. The bunched field creates traffic problems but also opportunities for those who time their runs perfectly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tactics Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If Align The Stars or Bahadur press forward earlier than expected.
scenarios.body: The Johnston runner's recent form edge or Bahadur's hat-trick confidence translates to more aggressive positioning. They avoid the inevitable late scramble and maintain momentum when it matters.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If Kihavah goes too slow and creates a cavalry charge finish.
scenarios.body: The race becomes a messy sprint finish where positioning trumps ability. Dramatic Star's first-time headgear or Brasil Power's stamina reserves could prove decisive in a blanket finish.

watchPoints.text: Kihavah getting uncontested lead could prove decisive given his tactical advantage and improved 2024 form in this very race
Track positioning turning into home straight as bunched field of hold-up horses will create traffic issues for late runners
Yashin and Subsequent both returning after 230+ day breaks but both have strong fresh records when fit
Align The Stars settling closer than usual given his recent aggressive tactics and current confidence levels
First-time headgear on Dramatic Star could spark improvement after two disappointing runs in 2026

races.name: Betfred 1000 Guineas Stakes (Group 1) (Fillies)

runners_data.name: My Highness
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with strong finishing kick, benefits from strong gallop, trainer Fabre excellent with Classic fillies
runners_data.comment: Similar profile to the same yard's winner of this race in 2014; may well resume progress
runners_data.spotlight: Ended her 2yo campaign with quite a tidy success in Group 2 at Deauville (7f, good) to complete a hat-trick; beaten favourite (finished second, splitting outsiders) in the Prix Imprudence over the same C&D on reappearance but that was also the case with the same yard's Miss France, who rebounded to land this prize in 2014; likely to be suited by stepping up to 1m; enters calculations, with a resumption of improvement plausible.

runners_data.name: Abashiri
runners_data.note: Hold-up style on seasonal debut after 179 days off, needs the run but Appleby/Buick combination always respected
runners_data.comment: Well bred; quickened smartly for an impressive win at Kempton; brings major potential
runners_data.spotlight: Well-bred filly, by Frankel out of a 1m2f Group 1 scorer for her connections; quickened smartly and recorded an impressive 4l success in Kempton maiden (1m, AW) six months ago; the shortest on experience, being the sole once-raced contender, but brings major potential; interesting.

runners_data.name: Domina Ignis
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with similar profile to 2024 winner Elmalka, recent run suggests fitness edge
runners_data.comment: Good third in the Fred Darling; very similar profile to Elmalka, who won this race in 2024
runners_data.spotlight: Very similar profile to the 2024 Guineas winner Elmalka, having won at Southwell in sole 2yo start then finished third in the Fred Darling (Group 3); gained her success (6f, AW) in emphatic fashion despite taking a good hold, then was beaten only 2l with hood fitted at Newbury (7f, good) despite being hampered; bred to stay 1m and looks open to further progress.

runners_data.name: Silenciosa
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer from small yard, lacks the class edge but Tom Clover horses often outrun odds
runners_data.comment: Nice prospect for Tom Clover but this assignment demands plenty of further progress
runners_data.spotlight: Scored with something to spare at Southwell (AW) in sole 2yo start, then did well to finish sixth in the Fred Darling at Newbury (again over 7f) having been slowly away, met traffic issues and been forced to switch; remains a nice prospect for Tom Clover but this assignment demands another big leap forward on bare figures.

runners_data.name: Precise
runners_data.note: Classic hold-up style with proven Group 1 winning form at the track, long absence a concern at 205 days
runners_data.comment: Continued her excellent progress with comfortable win in the Fillies' Mile; leading player
runners_data.spotlight: Excellent progress last term culminated in Group 1 wins at the Curragh (7f, yielding) and Newmarket, bringing up a four-timer; drew clear inside the final 1f and comfortably beat Venetian Lace by just over 3l in the Fillies' Mile over C&D (good) on the final occasion; had a minor setback to her schedule with a slightly raised temperature in March but is apparently fine now; trainer has landed this race seven times; leading contender.

runners_data.name: True Love
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who can adapt tactics, excellent recent Newmarket form and proven at the distance
runners_data.comment: Cheveley Park Stakes winner; has a largely solid record; one of the main contenders
runners_data.spotlight: In the same ball park as stablemate Precise on ratings and, like that filly, is a Group 1 winner at Newmarket (Cheveley Park Stakes over 6f); landed the Queen Mary at Royal Ascot (5f) earlier in her 2yo campaign and added a Group 3 prize, with something to spare, at Leopardstown (7f, good to yielding) on reappearance; has a solid record aside from an excusable defeat at the Breeders' Cup; upped further in trip and has stamina on the dam's side; one of the main players.

runners_data.name: Rose Ghaiyyath
runners_data.note: Prominent style but long layoff of 234 days makes her hard to assess on seasonal debut
runners_data.comment: Showed her 2yo promise on softer than good; interesting if the ground is similar
runners_data.spotlight: Has something to find at this level but is open to further improvement and would be particularly interesting if the ground is on the soft side, having shown her 2yo promise on slower than good, namely a narrow success in newcomers' event at Deauville (7f) and a rallying fourth in the May Hill at Doncaster (1m Group 2).

runners_data.name: Inis Mor
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with solid course form, will ensure genuine pace but stamina questioned at the trip
runners_data.comment: Solid 2yo form; may take a step forward with Nell Gwyn reappearance under her belt
runners_data.spotlight: Solid 2yo form with two novice wins on the Newmarket July course and a good second in valuable conditions race at Longchamp (sole 1m attempt); didn't particularly boost her Guineas claims with 2l fourth to Asleet in the Nell Gwyn (7f, good) but she may take a step forward with that reappearance outing under her belt.

runners_data.name: The Prettiest Star
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner with tactical pace, long absence of 219 days but Walker stable in good form
runners_data.comment: Clear second in the Rockfel; possibilities with further improvement on the cards
runners_data.spotlight: Daughter of her connections' July Cup winner Starman; duly showed plenty of promise in both 2yo starts, recording a clearcut success at Nottingham (6f, good) and close second, clear of remainder, in the Rockfel at Newmarket (7f, good to firm; Group 2); gives the impression she'll be suited by this further step up in distance; possibilities with additional improvement on the cards.

runners_data.name: Venetian Sun
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who stays well, absence since October but excellent course record suggests readiness
runners_data.comment: Below-form 3rd to Precise on final 2yo effort but 4-4 previously; may well resume progress
runners_data.spotlight: Absent since finishing third to Precise in the Moyglare Stud Stakes when upped to 7f at the Curragh, losing her unbeaten record but far from disgraced and sticking on in a manner that suggests she'll stay 1m this year; 4-4 previously and completed a notable 6f hat-trick with wins in Group 3 at Royal Ascot, Group 2 at Newmarket (July) and Group 1 at Deauville; may well rate higher still and add to an already impressive tally; pleased her trainer in a racecourse gallop last month; highly respected.

runners_data.name: Evolutionist
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with strong recent form, second string from Burke stable but capable of big performance
runners_data.comment: Strong at the finish in Group 3 at Longchamp, showing that she has trained on well
runners_data.spotlight: Newmarket form comprises a maiden win on the July course and third-place finish, just over 4l behind Precise, in the Group 1 Fillies' Mile; bagged Group 3 honours at Longchamp (1m, good) on reappearance, collaring a sitting duck (clear leader who tired) and strong at the finish; has evidently trained on well and her RPRs continue on an upward trajectory.

runners_data.name: Darn Hot Gallop
runners_data.note: Hold-up style who won at the course and distance recently, lacks the class but could outrun odds
runners_data.comment: Won C&D handicap at the Craven meeting, taking record to 3-3; this is much harder
runners_data.spotlight: From the family of Enable; edged ahead close home in C&D handicap (good; ran off a mark of 83) at the Craven meeting, adding to her 2yo AW wins; it's hard to knock an improving filly who remains unbeaten (3-3) but her form is a long way short of Classic standard, as BHA ratings reflect.

runners_data.name: Venetian Lace
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who surprised in Fillies Mile, needs to prove that effort was genuine form
runners_data.comment: Needs to prove she can back up the form of her big-priced second in the Fillies' Mile
runners_data.spotlight: Belied market position (rank outsider) by finishing second to Precise in the Group 1 Fillies' Mile over C&D but needs to prove she can back up that apparent improvement; may be flattered by her new rating and, combined with a record of 0-5 since debut success, doesn't look a solid contestant.

runners_data.name: Mubasimah
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner who races exclusively at Newmarket, will set strong pace but stamina concerns at the trip
runners_data.comment: Only sixth when favourite for the Nell Gwyn; low in calculations after that effort
runners_data.spotlight: Frankel filly who has been campaigned exclusively over 7f at Newmarket, producing good performances (won maiden and second in Group 3) from the front last autumn and then not asked to lead when only sixth, beaten favourite, in the Nell Gwyn; may still have more to offer but this is a difficult task in terms of form and tactical considerations.

runners_data.name: Touleen
runners_data.note: Prominent style with solid recent form, Saffie Osborne booking suggests confidence from connections
runners_data.comment: Satisfactory reappearance in the Fred Darling; from the family of a 1,000 Guineas winner
runners_data.spotlight: Gained her 2yo wins in stylish fashion and made a satisfactory reappearance as favourite for the Fred Darling at Newbury (7f, good; Group 3) when a close second under Saffie Osborne; bit to prove back at Newmarket, having looked ill at ease here in the Rockfel, but a plausible danger provided she handles the track better this time; from the family of 1,000 Guineas winner Ghanaati and retains potential.

runners_data.name: Spicy Marg
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who has been campaigned mainly as sprinter, stepping up in trip is questionable
runners_data.comment: Useful sprinter last season; has doubts over the new trip and the deeper waters
runners_data.spotlight: Proved a useful sprinter last season, notably winning over 5f at Glorious Goodwood in the summer and over 6f at Newmarket (beat Azleet in good-ground Listed contest) final outing; not an obvious 1,000 Guineas player, with doubts over the new trip and the deeper waters (she's a stone below the standard required).

runners_data.name: Azleet
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with course-winning form, upset winner last time suggests she can defy odds again
runners_data.comment: Won the Nell Gwyn but doesn't look a budding star and may well come up short
runners_data.spotlight: Belied her 50-1 odds with neck success in the Nell Gwyn (upped to 7f, good; Group 3) on seasonal debut, taking strike-rate to 3-8 and form figures on the Newmarket tracks to 121; doesn't look a budding star and only two fillies in the last 40 years have landed that trial then followed up in the 1,000 Guineas; may well come up short.

runners_data.name: True Test
runners_data.note: Hold-up style but exposed form suggests she lacks the class required for this level
runners_data.comment: Went close in the Jumeirah 1,000 Guineas at Meydan; this is a much stronger race
runners_data.spotlight: Career commenced with two wins, the second one on the Newmarket July course; record of 0-5 since reflects that her limitations are rather exposed, and this is a markedly stronger Guineas than the Jumeirah 1,000 Guineas in which she went close at Meydan (1m, good; Listed) last time.

runners_data.name: Timeforshowcasing
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who stays well, recent Newcastle win on all-weather suggests fitness advantage
runners_data.comment: Has built up a good-strike rate but looks out of her depth at this level
runners_data.spotlight: Held on gamely in 1m Listed event at Newcastle on seasonal debut, taking AW record to 2-2 and overall strike-rate to 4-6; may win more races at the right level but looks out of her depth in this company returned to turf, as her two defeats (both Group 2) attest.

races.paceDynamic: The Prettiest Star, Mubasimah, and Inis Mor will ensure a genuine gallop from the outset, with all three having confirmed front-running tendencies and the tactical speed to dictate terms. Their combined presence guarantees strong early fractions that will stretch the field and test stamina reserves over this stiff mile. The sustained pace will drag the prominent runners forward and create gaps for the hold-up horses to exploit in the final two furlongs. This genuine pace scenario strongly favours hold-up performers who can quicken off a solid gallop and punishes those who need to be handy early.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Suits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners maintain their duel through halfway and beyond
scenarios.body: The sustained gallop will tire the early leaders and stretch the field, creating perfect conditions for horses with finishing kicks to sweep through. Hold-up performers like Precise, My Highness, and Evolutionist will have ideal conditions to unleash their acceleration.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Gets Away
scenarios.trigger: If one of the pace-setters establishes a decisive advantage while the others falter early
scenarios.body: The winner will steal crucial lengths before the field realizes the danger, making the deficit too great for the closers to bridge. This scenario rewards the front-runner with the best tactical speed and stamina combination.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Profits
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes unsustainably fast and burns out all three front-runners
scenarios.body: The race will fall to a horse positioned just behind the leaders who can inherit the lead and stay on strongly. Those tracking in second or third position will be perfectly placed to capitalize on the pace collapse.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Early
scenarios.trigger: If all three front-runners are pulled back or fail to maintain their usual tactics
scenarios.body: The race becomes a tactical affair with no genuine pace, turning into a sprint finish that favours horses with natural speed over stamina. This unlikely scenario would completely change the complexion of the contest.

watchPoints.text: The Prettiest Star and Mubasimah must both go forward early or the pace scenario changes completely
Precise's 205-day layoff is a significant concern for a filly who needs to be spot-on fitness-wise
True Love's versatile running style allows tactical flexibility if the pace scenario develops differently
Abashiri represents the Godolphin team on seasonal debut with fitness queries after winter break
Watch for Azleet's early positioning as she upset the field last time when getting the perfect trip

races.name: Tattersalls £40,000 EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Crownbreaker
runners_data.comment: 550,000gns half-sister to July Cup winner Mill Stream; yard off mark with 2yos; contender
runners_data.spotlight: March foal; 550,000gns yearling; fourth foal; Minzaal half-sister to winners Mill Stream (6f including 2yo/Group 1 July Cup; RPR 120) and Asymmetric (5f/6f including 2yo Group 2; 109); dam 5f/6f winner (including 2yo; 83); strong paper claims for a trainer who is already off the mark with his 2yos.

runners_data.name: Donna Beauty
runners_data.comment: 35,000gns half-sister to 4 winners out of a useful German mare; not obviously precocious
runners_data.spotlight: March foal; 35,000gns yearling; seventh foal; Starspangledbanner half-sister to four winners including Grocer Jack (1m2f/10.5f including German/Italian Group 3; RPR 116) and Ghislaine (7f-8.7f including Listed; 99); dam German 1m-1m3f winner (including Group 3; 104); not obviously precocious on paper but worth a market check.

runners_data.name: Efsixteen
runners_data.comment: 350,000gns breeze-up 2yo; sharp pedigree and makes debut for an in-form trainer
runners_data.spotlight: Late April foal by Havana Grey; 135,000gns yearling, 350,000gns breeze-up 2yo; eighth foal; sister to 5f/6f winner Pilgrim (including 2yo; RPR 106), half-sister to winners Moraawed (6f/7f; 92) and Crash Helmet (6f AW; 71); dam 5f 2yo winner (74), half-sister to 6f 2yo Group 2 winner Temple Meads; looks the part on paper and she makes her debut with her yard in form.

runners_data.name: Havana Sprite
runners_data.comment: 150,000gns yearling; half-sister to a minor 5f 2yo winner; dam a winning 2yo; check market
runners_data.spotlight: January foal; 150,000gns yearling; second foal; Havana Grey half-sister to 5f 2yo winner Polly Darling (RPR 71); dam 6f/6.5f 2yo winner (93); stable 0-2 with their 2yos this year but had one run well behind Call Me Tomorrow last month.

runners_data.name: Holi Scarlett
runners_data.comment: 17,000euros yearling; bred to be sharp but could be starting out in a hot race
runners_data.spotlight: April foal by Bungle Inthejungle; 17,000euros yearling; sixth foal; sister to 5f/6f winner Lily In The Jungle (including 2yo; RPR 74), half-sister to 5f 2yo winner Lili Wen Fach (69); dam 5f winner (71), out of half-sister to 5f 2yo Group 3 winner Show Me The Money; bred to have a future but she is starting out in a potentially hot contest.

runners_data.name: Lazurite
runners_data.comment: £175,000 yearling with five winning siblings; dam a Listed winner; a newcomer of note
runners_data.spotlight: March foal by Blue Point; £175,000 yearling; closely related to 6f-1m winner Hallasan (including 2yo; RPR 99), half-sister to four winners including Al Raya (5f 2yo including Group 3; 105), Grisons (5f-6f; 79) and Mystify Me (5f; 70); dam 5f and 6f (Listed) 2yo winner (99); trainer has had a winning 2yo newcomer this year; William Buick booked.

runners_data.name: Call Me Tomorrow
runners_data.comment: Shaped well when second over C&D last month; leading claims with progress likely
runners_data.spotlight: Weak 9-1 shot for her C&D debut 18 days ago but she made a bold bid, travelling strongly but finding one too strong in the closing stages; that effort was backed up by the Topspeed figure and she sets a useful standard for the newcomers to aim at before factoring in progress.

runners_data.name: Pageant Girl
runners_data.comment: Stepped up on Beverley debut when winning at Ripon (6f, good) 8 days ago; this is tougher
runners_data.spotlight: Promise amid inexperience on her Beverley debut (5f, good to soft) and still looked a work in progress when winning a 6f novice at Ripon eight days ago; had the benefit of the rail to help her but she kept on well enough; she will need to progress again to defy a penalty against some interesting opposition, though.

races.name: Tattersalls Online £40,000 EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Agamemnon
runners_data.comment: 150,000gns breeze-up 2yo; dam once-raced 2yo winner; William Buick booked; check betting
runners_data.spotlight: February foal by Mehmas; £72,000 yearling, 150,000gns breeze-up 2yo; first foal of a once-raced 7f 2yo winner (RPR 89); trainer off the mark with 2yos this year; William Buick booked; market confidence would look significant.

runners_data.name: Beauty For Love
runners_data.comment: 130,000euros yearling with four winning siblings; dam a useful 1m winner; can't dismiss
runners_data.spotlight: March foal by Blue Point; 140,000euros foal, 130,000euros yearling; sixth foal; closely related to Italian 7.5f-1m2f winner Conquering Eagle, half-brother to winners Apricot Ice (6f; RPR 95), Saraqael (1m; 93) and Seasony (7f/1m including 2yo/AW/Czechia; 79); dam Group-placed 1m winner (100); enough paper appeal to warrant a second look.

runners_data.name: Persian Spring
runners_data.comment: 100,000gns yearling; three winning siblings (inc Group 3); powerful yard; shortlisted
runners_data.spotlight: April foal; 100,000gns yearling by Persian Force; eighth foal; closely related to 6f 2yo winner Beauty Inspire (including Group 3; RPR 102), half-brother to winners Darwell Lion (7f-8.6f including 2yo/AW; 97) and Camera Shy (6f/7f including 2yo/AW; 78); dam French 1m4f winner, out of 5f/6f winner; represents a powerful yard; shortlisted.

runners_data.name: The Dancing Pirate
runners_data.comment: Dam a smart 6f/7f winner; appeal on paper but he's a late foal for early-season 2yo races
runners_data.spotlight: May 28 foal by Blackbeard; third foal of a smart 6f/7f winner (including Group 3; RPR 106), herself from an excellent family; should have a future but comfortably the youngest of these and he will need to be useful to make a winning start.

runners_data.name: Jaan Ki Tukri
runners_data.comment: Pleasing 3rd at Newbury on debut (green off the bridle; neck in front of Napa); contender
runners_data.spotlight: Promise amid inexperience when third of nine in a 5f maiden (good ground) at Newbury 16 days ago, racing freely early on and paying the price in the closing stages; finished a neck in front of Napa on that occasion and can confirm the placings.

runners_data.name: Napa
runners_data.comment: Sent off favourite for his debut and ran creditably for 4th (a neck behind Jaan Ki Turki)
runners_data.spotlight: Sent off favourite for his Newbury debut 16 days ago (5f, good) and ran creditably, not helped by being a bit tight for room inside the final furlong; finished a neck behind Jaan Ki Tukri on that occasion and he is no banker to reverse the placings.

runners_data.name: Noble Raider
runners_data.comment: Pushed along throughout when never-dangerous 2nd at Wolverhampton 12 days ago; yard run 2
runners_data.spotlight: Always on the back foot on his Wolverhampton debut 12 days ago (5f) and although he ran on for second, he was no threat to the easy winner; should have learned from that initial experience but connections look to hold stronger claims with Napa.

races.name: HKJC World Pool Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Sahara King
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who showed marked improvement when winning at Wolverhampton but faces much stronger opposition stepping up in class
runners_data.comment: AW win on debut; late gains for close 5th in hot Newbury novice (1m2f, good) 16 days ago
runners_data.spotlight: 16-1 for novice at Wolverhampton (8.6f, AW) in November but always prominent and led final strides; 14-1 in a hot novice at Newbury (1m2f, good) 16 days ago and made late gains to finish on heels of the leaders in a blanket finish; set for further improvement and likely to prove better than this opening mark at some point soon.

runners_data.name: Study Of Words
runners_data.note: Classy prominent runner returning from 193-day break but Charlie Appleby's 1/20 record over past 14 days is concerning
runners_data.comment: Beat a fair maiden 15l to win four-runner maiden at 1-7 over C&D (good) on final 2yo start
runners_data.spotlight: Marked improvement through three-race 2yo career, beating a fair maiden by 15l when he won a four-runner maiden at 1-7 over C&D (good) final start; that can't be the most solid form but he could hardly have done it more easily and is a Derby entry; fascinating handicap debutant in first-time headgear.

runners_data.name: Gatehouse
runners_data.note: Only hold-up runner in the field but all form is on AW surfaces, making turf debut a question mark
runners_data.comment: A 2nd and two wins on AW; return to 1m2f should suit and further improvement is possible
runners_data.spotlight: All three runs were on AW, with plenty of promise on debut before he won a novice at Chelmsford (1m2f) in December and seven-runner handicap by a short head at Southwell (1m) in April; return to 1m2f should suit and, although he's been raised 4lb, further improvement is possible.

runners_data.name: Evanesco
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits but weakened badly in final furlong on seasonal debut 18 days ago over course and distance
runners_data.comment: Second favourite for handicap/seasonal debut over C&D but weakened into fourth of eight
runners_data.spotlight: Pretty useful in two of his five efforts as 2yo; second favourite for handicap/seasonal debut over C&D (good) 18 days ago but weakened in the final 1f into fourth of eight; that was creditable but he needs to build on it.

runners_data.name: Crockham Heath
runners_data.note: Confirmed front runner who won two AW races but 93 days since last run and modest topspeed rating of 41 raises stamina doubts
runners_data.comment: Well beaten here on debut; won twice on AW, with authority last time; could be useful
runners_data.spotlight: Well beaten at 50-1 on debut here (7f, good) in October; way better, however, for front-running wins in a Southwell novice (1m) in November and seven-runner handicap at Wolverhampton (9.4f) in January; those wins were AW but with authority last time (8lb higher today) and he could be a useful prospect.

races.paceDynamic: Crockham Heath is the only confirmed front runner in this small field and should get an uncontested lead, setting a steady gallop over the 1m2f trip. The prominent runners Sahara King, Study Of Words, and Evanesco will likely settle just behind the leader, while hold-up horse Gatehouse tracks from the rear. With no pace pressure on Crockham Heath early, this sets up as a tactical affair where the final 2-3 furlongs will be crucial. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners who can track the leader and kick clear, as they get the best of both worlds - cover from the pace but close enough to strike when the tempo lifts.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent trio can track Crockham Heath comfortably and the pace stays steady until the 2f pole
scenarios.body: Study Of Words and Sahara King get perfect trips behind the leader and can unleash superior finishing kicks. Evanesco also benefits from this tactical setup despite recent disappointing form.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Crockham Heath gets soft fractions and the prominent horses fail to coordinate their challenge
scenarios.body: The leader builds an unassailable advantage and holds on despite modest finishing speed. His two AW wins suggest stamina for the trip when getting his own way.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is stronger than expected or the prominent runners go too early
scenarios.body: Gatehouse gets the perfect setup from his patient style as the pace collapses in front of him. His recent AW form translates well to this tactical scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If all runners are overly cautious and the race becomes a crawling affair until very late
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure sprint finish where class tells and Study Of Words' superior rating shows. However, this scenario suits no one perfectly and creates chaos.

watchPoints.text: Study Of Words' market support despite long layoff and poor trainer form - if backed heavily suggests hidden fitness
Crockham Heath's early fractions - if he goes too fast early he'll compromise his stamina advantage
Gatehouse's position turning for home - needs to be within 3-4 lengths to have any chance from his hold-up style
Evanesco's finishing kick at the 2f pole - showed concerning signs of stopping last time at this course
Sahara King's position with a furlong to run - inexperienced but talented enough to cause an upset if getting perfect trip
